source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1924, p. 5 ("Antrim County Council: unopposed returns in nineteen divisions; the first lady member")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed: the only candidate nominated (Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1924: nineteen divisions unopposed)

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council on the 23 county electoral divisions; nominations received by Alexander Millar, secretary and returning officer, at the County Courthouse, Belfast, on 7 May 1924. Nineteen divisions were returned unopposed (thirteen retiring members and six new members, among them Mrs Anna E. Barbour for Dunmurry, the council's first woman member); polls in Ahoghill, Antrim, Ballymena and Ballymoney on Thursday 5 June 1924, counted at the County Courthouse, Crumlin Road, the next morning (Belfast News-Letter, 8 and 15 May and 7 June 1924). The nominations list prints no party labels, so none are given. Returned unopposed.
